subtitle: Red chile enchiladas with queso fresco
verso: Dip it in the chile and fry it on the spot: that's how a living is got.
story: Tortillas dipped in red chile, fried and rolled around cheese and onion. In Guanajuato they come topped with fried potatoes and carrots: enchiladas mineras, said to be what miners' wives carried up to the mines. In Real del Monte, Hidalgo, the mineras are made with salsa verde.

ingredients.title: The enchiladas
items: 2 cups crumbled queso fresco (or queso ranchero)

ingredients.title: On top
items: 2 potatoes and 2 carrots, diced and boiled
A piece of fried chicken, optional

steps: Toast and soak the chiles. Blend with the garlic, onion, oregano, cumin and [[2 cups]] liquid. Strain.
Fry the sauce in the lard 5 minutes and season. It should be about as thick as cream. Keep warm.
Mix the cheese and onion for the filling, saving some for the top.
Heat ½ inch of oil in a skillet. Pass each tortilla through the warm sauce, then fry it 10 seconds per side. (For less splatter, fry first and then dip.)
Fill with cheese and onion, roll, and set on a plate.
Fry the boiled potatoes and carrots in the same oil until golden.
Top with more sauce, the potatoes and carrots, lettuce, pickled chiles, crema and the rest of the cheese.
pressureNote: No pressure-cooker version. Enchiladas are made at the skillet, one tortilla at a time.
tips: Work fast and serve right away. Enchiladas don't like to wait.

variations.name: Enfrijoladas
variations.subtitle: Tortillas in black bean sauce
variations.note: Tortillas bathed in a seasoned black bean sauce instead of chile.

items: 3 cups black pot beans (frijoles de la olla) with their broth
Queso fresco, crema and onion; shredded chicken optional

steps: Blend the beans with their broth, the chile and the avocado leaves until smooth, like thin cream.
Fry the tortillas lightly, dip them in the bean sauce, and fold in quarters or fill with cheese or chicken.
Top with crema, cheese and onion.
